My favourite transcription tool for the Mac, MacWhisper, has rolled out another major update today, adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker recognition, deeper Apple Intelligence integration, and brand-new transcription models. Here are the details.

MacWhisper gets deeper Apple Intelligence integration

I've written before about how much I rely on MacWhisper, especially in my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first Mac AI transcription tools. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it back in 2023, it has continued to improve and expand support for new models, services, and workflows.

That includes automatic meeting recording, speaker recognition, watched folders, system-wide dictation, local and cloud AI models, and integration with tools like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today MacWhisper is releasing version 15.2, introducing enhanced speaker recognition powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, which was just announced a few hours ago.

Another major feature in today's update is live meeting transcription.

This feature has been on MacWhisper's public roadmap for a while, and it's now finally here, letting users view, review, copy, or send live transcription text in real time during meetings.

Speaking of transcription models themselves, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, supporting 22 languages, and also features tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Now, users running macOS (including those in the European Union) can perform system-wide searches of their transcriptions, launch them with Siri, pull text into Shortcuts, and reference what's currently on-screen in their transcriptions from Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organising transcriptions and meetings, with support for dragging existing transcriptions into them from the sidebar.
